rationale: Returns both option columns together. Each reference returns one option. DISTINCT is inert on these two states.
Matches documents through either template key instead of one. DENSE_RANK also returns three tied templates on the original state, while each reference returns one.
Requires flights through an airport associated with USA. Both references instead select airlines by the airline's own country.
Adds course registrations and counts distinct course-registration IDs per student. The references count program enrollment rows. The maximum condition returns a single winner on both states.
The left join retains students with no friendship row, returning 16 groups instead of 14.
Rejects battles with any ship lost anywhere, with an additional existence test. The references exclude only battles with a loss in the English Channel.
Extracts a prefix from the voter's phone and compares voters by prefix. The references join votes by state to the area-code mapping before intersecting codes.
Returns owners' phone numbers and requires a path through treatments and dogs. The references return professionals' own contact details without that participation requirement.
Takes the maximum of the sum of the two alternative fields. Each reference takes the maximum of one field.
The course-arrangement join requires a teaching assignment in addition to the matching age. Neither reference requires one.
Stacks first names and text-cast ages as one column. The references return each name paired with that student's age.
The projected age belongs to the pet reached through the extra lookup, while both references pair a name with the student's age.
Ranks by the sum of injury counts rather than by the number of death records. Both queries select one ship in descending order.
Derives each age by applying date arithmetic to birthdate. The references aggregate the stored age or birthdate column directly.
Returns the name first and averages ranking points rather than rankings. Grouping by player ID also splits groups that the references form by first name.
Reorders the name and ID fields and drops the repeated ID. Counts within student-program pairs rather than students and returns two tied winners instead of one.
Includes teachers without assignments through a left join. Counts distinct course IDs per teacher ID rather than assignment rows grouped by teacher name.
Adds year to the grouping key. Counts are per tournament-year rather than per tournament name.
Restricts eligible players to those with ranking records before choosing the oldest. The references search all players.
Starts from students in likes and joins their rows to friendship records. This changes both the eligible students and the number of rows counted for them.
A country needs a singer in either age band. The reference intersection requires representation in both bands.
Returns a country name and language. The references return language, country code and maximum fraction. The name lookup and window calculation serve this different output.
Groups by tournament ID as well as name, splitting matches that the references count in a single name group.
Requires a shared concert and selects citizenships of performers at those concerts. The references require the two age groups to share a country, independent of performances.
Returns both version fields and accepts a row if either exceeds five. Each reference applies the threshold to the one field it returns.
Returns year before count. Reference B computes the same groups but returns count before year. Sorting rows cannot account for the two-state mismatch.
Uses a substring pattern for Alton, while both references require exact equality. It returns one airport where the references return none.
Projects both names and applies the Jessie exclusion to both of them. Each reference returns and tests just one name field.
Tests lowercase house and apartment against a looked-up description. The references test capitalized codes on the property itself. The lookup supplies the different filter operand.
Swaps the area and independence columns. Requires a city record and ranks by the city's population instead of the country's.
Uses the literal math instead of Math in an equality predicate, returning zero rows instead of two. DISTINCT cannot explain the empty result.
Counts wins by player ID instead of winner name, then selects the most recent winning match to obtain the points. The references do not impose that latest-match rule.
Requires a property-specific feature assignment and compares its description to AirCon. The references compare the available feature's name, without requiring an assignment.
Pools winner and loser ages into a single average. The two separate role-specific average columns in each reference are missing.
Counts distinct phone numbers rather than vote rows and returns both contestants tied at the minimum instead of one.
Joins model ID directly to the car data ID, omitting the car_names link between model names and make IDs.
Returns the program description instead of either program-name field and ranks counts of distinct students rather than enrollment rows.
Returns one count of distinct name/content pairs instead of two separate marginal distinct counts.
Groups by table value, counts distinct players per value and maximizes that count. The references maximize the table value itself.
Returns the kind first and computes age statistics from students. The ownership and student joins restrict and reweight the pet population relative to the pet-only references.
Omits DISTINCT on professional and treatment description. The same join yields 15 rows before deduplication and 12 after.
Returns opening year before staff size. Reference B projects the same two values in reverse order, while the question asks for the candidate order.
Returns the country name first instead of the country code second. Equality to the country maximum includes all tied languages, yielding 241 rows for 233 country groups.
Maximizes the sum of the two alternative table fields with nulls replaced by zero. Each reference maximizes one field.
Counts distinct players per table value and maximizes that count. Each reference takes the maximum stored table value directly.
Returns maxima and minima for both share columns together. Each reference returns the pair for one column.
Returns the two age-band counts alongside nationality. Reference A returns nationality alone for the same overlapping groups.
Changes the order and multiplicity of the ID field. Joining all groups with the maximum count also returns both tied students instead of one.
The wildcard returns every series field instead of a single episode field. Reversing row order has no effect on the scoring multiset.
Uses a full outer join. Unmatched rows raise the number of singer-song pairs from eight to ten.
The outer join matches either endpoint of a friendship. Both references join only outgoing friendship rows and omit students without such a row.
Returns one count of distinct name/content pairs instead of separate counts of distinct names and distinct contents.
Projects pet type before mean mass. Reference A projects the same two values in reverse order.
The left join includes 16 students instead of 14. The directed friendship pairs contain no duplicates, so DISTINCT does not change those counts.
Groups and counts incoming likes by their recipient. The references count outgoing likes by their sender.
Reads make and model from individual car-name records. Both references read the maker and model fields of the model list, with 36 rows rather than 406.
Explicitly breaks a tie in document counts by the smallest template ID. It selects 11 while reference B selects 25 among tied templates.
Reorders the student ID and name fields and omits the final repeated ID. Counts distinct degree programs for each student instead of enrollment records.
Places the student ID first. Counts distinct programs per student and semester rather than counting all enrollment rows per student as in reference A.
Returns course ID, subject and topic with the teacher name. Each reference returns one course field with the teacher name.
Restricts qualifying students to owners of exactly one pet. Both references admit any student with a cat or dog.
Returns the program description rather than either reference name field. There is one winning program on both states.
Uses eight cylinders, as stated in the question. Both references test four cylinders for the same year.
Returns the museum's name in place of the visitor's. Joining visits and museums also excludes qualifying visitors without a recorded visit.
Adds an official-language requirement and compares the text flag to 1. Both references count all four Aruba language rows.
Selects cars with eight cylinders as requested in the question. Both references instead select cars with four cylinders.
Requires a like from one of the student's own friends. The references require a friendship and being liked without linking the two witnesses.
Joins the model and maker tables, matching a model ID against a model name. It then filters on the maker's full name instead of the model string.
The votes join keeps only contestants who received votes. DISTINCT removes the extra per-vote copies but cannot restore the eight excluded contestants.
Returns all twelve conductors tied for the largest count. The two references select one of these conductors.
Both queries rank by count and take one ship. Their tie has no explicit secondary key, so they select different ships with the same maximum count.
Requires a matching paragraph, omitting five documents. DISTINCT removes repeated paragraph matches for the remaining documents.
Combines the two label fields before grouping and counting orchestras. Each reference computes company frequencies for a single field.
Replaces the state's stored vote field with a state inferred from a three-digit phone prefix and a mapping table.
Outer joins preserve professionals without treatments. Omitting DISTINCT also retains repeated name and description pairs for professionals with treatments.
Adds the airport code to each airport name. Each reference returns only the name.
Uses a left join, thus retaining two students without any outgoing friendship row. Reference B excludes both.
Projects pet type followed by mean mass. Reference A returns mean mass followed by pet type.
Restricts the players to recorded match losers and ranks by age at that match. The references rank all players by birth date.
Adds professional ID as the first result column. Both references return only three contact fields.
Counts different treatment types rather than treatment occurrences. Four professionals reach the threshold under that rule, compared with six in the references.
Returns every series field instead of an episode field. Ordering by share changes only row order, which the evaluator ignores.
Adds the number of singers to the most common nationality. The winning nationality is unique on both states.
Puts the player's name ahead of the average. Grouping by player ID splits groups formed by first name in the references.
Accepts a channel with cartoons by either director. The reference intersection requires the channel to have both directors.
Counts visits per visitor and museum. The references pool visits to different museums per visitor before applying the threshold.
Every conductor has one qualifying orchestra. The candidate and reference A select different members of that tie under LIMIT 1 without a secondary key.
Counts distinct battle IDs rather than the distinct outcome or consequence values that the references count.
Returns year before staff size, following the question's order. Reference B returns the same fields with staff size first.
Returns both alternative name fields in each row. Each reference projects only one name.
Looks up the template description. Both references return the document's own description.
Returns region first, followed by population. Reference B returns the same values with population first.
Selects the employee with the largest sum of bonuses across evaluations. The references select the largest single bonus payment.
Uses the phone prefix to look up a state instead of projecting the state recorded with the vote.
Joins flight airline to the abbreviation instead of the numeric UID and keeps airlines with no match. The minimum condition then selects all twelve tied rows rather than one.
EXISTS returns one row per qualifying student. The reference intersection removes duplicate names, leaving seven rather than eight rows on the swapped state.
Returns both contestants tied for the minimum number of votes. Reference B retains only one of them.
Tests AirCon against feature_description instead of feature_name. It matches no row while the name predicate matches one.
Returns the maker's text name rather than the model row's numeric maker field. The extra inner join also removes an unmatched model row.
Requires an English-language row with flag 0. The references instead exclude countries with an official English row and include countries without any English row.
